Context/Background:
Intraductal papillary neoplasms (IPNs),  including intraductal papillary mucinous neoplasms (IPMNs), intraductal oncocytic papillary neoplasms (IOPNs), and intraductal tubulopapillary neoplasms (ITPNs), are clinically detectable macroscopic non-invasive cyst-forming lesions, some of which progress to invasive pancreatic cancer. Proteins and glycoproteins have proven to be useful clinical biomarkers for classifying cyst-forming neoplasms in the pancreas.Here, we used proteomics and glycoproteomics to characterize a series of histologically and genetically well-characterized surgically resected IPNs, including IPMNs and IOPNs.

Our analysis included 69 IPNs (64 IPMNs and 5 IOPNs), 76 macro-dissected grossly normal duct tissues (NDs, with 32 of the 76 NDs coming from the same resection specimens as the IPNs), and 32 cyst fluid samples (22 from matched IPMN patients, 3 matched IOPN patients, 2 from unrelated IPMN patients, and 5 other cysts).
Prompt: Compare the differential genes on global proteome level and glycoproteome level for IPMN vs ND.  Provide a pathway level summary of biological functions of upregulated or downregulated glycopeptides whose global protein expression remained unchanged.
output_text:
Introduction/Context  
- Lesions: Intraductal papillary mucinous neoplasms (IPMNs, n=64) and intraductal oncocytic papillary neoplasms (IOPNs, n=5) vs macro-dissected normal ducts (NDs, n=76; 32 matched).  
- Tissue: Pancreatic duct epithelium.  
- Assays: Global proteome (Table S2A) and glycoproteome (Table S3I).  
- Contrast: IPMN vs ND.  
- Key signals: 3 949 proteins significantly altered at FDR<0.05; 85 glycopeptides (57 genes) significantly changed at FDR<0.05. Of those, 18 glyco-altered proteins showed no global abundance change (FDR≥0.05).  

Keywords  
- Glycosylation  
- Sterol metabolism  
- Arginine catabolism  
- Protein secretion  
- Vesicle transport  

Candidate Genes  
- CPD  
- DDAH1  
- ERLIN2  
- GUSB  
- ATP6V0A2  

Pathway Enrichments (GSEA of glycopeptides up/down despite unchanged protein levels)  
Ratios per library (up/down):  
- KEGG_2016: 1 up (14%), 6 down (86%), ratio 0.17  
- GO_Biological_Process_2023: 34 up (52%), 31 down (48%), ratio 1.10  
- Reactome_Pathways_2024: 35 up (71%), 14 down (29%), ratio 2.50  
- MSigDB_Hallmark_2020: 4 up (57%), 3 down (43%), ratio 1.33  

KEGG_2016 (UP):  
| Theme                                      | Direction | Leading Genes |  
|--------------------------------------------|-----------|---------------|  
| Mucin type O-Glycan biosynthesis (hsa00512)| Up        | –             |  

KEGG_2016 (DOWN):  
| Theme                                           | Direction | Leading Genes            |  
|-------------------------------------------------|-----------|--------------------------|  
| Drug metabolism – other enzymes (hsa00983)      | Down      | GUSB                     |  
| Pentose and glucuronate interconversions (hsa00040)| Down    | GUSB                     |  
| Starch and sucrose metabolism (hsa00500)        | Down      | GUSB                     |  
| Glycosaminoglycan degradation (hsa00531)        | Down      | GUSB                     |  
| Lysosome (hsa04142)                             | Down      | GUSB, ATP6V0A2, GNPTAB   |  

GO_Biological_Process_2023 (UP):  
| Theme                                               | Direction | Leading Genes |  
|-----------------------------------------------------|-----------|---------------|  
| Protein Secretion (GO:0009306)                      | Up        | –             |  
| Insulin Secretion (GO:0030073)                      | Up        | –             |  
| Peptide Hormone Secretion (GO:0030072)              | Up        | –             |  
| Peptide Metabolic Process (GO:0006518)              | Up        | –             |  
| Negative Regulation Of Signal Transduction (GO:0009968)| Up    | –             |  

GO_Biological_Process_2023 (DOWN):  
| Theme                                          | Direction | Leading Genes |  
|------------------------------------------------|-----------|---------------|  
| Arginine Catabolic Process (GO:0006527)        | Down      | DDAH1         |  
| Protein Maturation (GO:0051604)                | Down      | CPD           |  
| Stress Fiber Assembly (GO:0043149)             | Down      | FAM171A1      |  
| Contractile Actin Filament Bundle Assembly (GO:0030038)| Down | FAM171A1 |  
| Actomyosin Structure Organization (GO:0031032)| Down      | FAM171A1      |  

Reactome_Pathways_2024 (UP):  
| Theme                             | Direction | Leading Genes |  
|-----------------------------------|-----------|---------------|  
| trans-Golgi Network Vesicle Budding| Up      | –             |  
| Vesicle-mediated Transport        | Up        | –             |  
| RND1 GTPase Cycle                 | Up        | –             |  
| Golgi Associated Vesicle Biogenesis| Up      | –             |  
| RND3 GTPase Cycle                 | Up        | –             |  

Reactome_Pathways_2024 (DOWN):  
| Theme                                           | Direction | Leading Genes |  
|-------------------------------------------------|-----------|---------------|  
| Metabolism of Nitric Oxide NOS3 Activation      | Down      | DDAH1         |  
| eNOS Activation                                 | Down      | DDAH1         |  
| RHO GTPase Cycle                                | Down      | CPD           |  
| Signaling by Rho GTPases, Miro GTPases and RHOBTB3| Down   | CPD           |  
| Signaling by Rho GTPases                        | Down      | CPD           |  

MSigDB_Hallmark_2020 (UP):  
| Theme                 | Direction | Leading Genes |  
|-----------------------|-----------|---------------|  
| Estrogen Response Late| Up        | –             |  
| KRAS Signaling Up     | Up        | –             |  
| UV Response Up        | Up        | –             |  
| Heme Metabolism       | Up        | –             |  

MSigDB_Hallmark_2020 (DOWN):  
| Theme                    | Direction | Leading Genes |  
|--------------------------|-----------|---------------|  
| Cholesterol Homeostasis  | Down      | GUSB          |  
| Glycolysis               | Down      | GUSB          |  
| UV Response Dn           | Down      | DDAH1         |  

Analysis  
These glycopeptide‐driven enrichments highlight upregulated secretory and O-glycan biosynthesis programs (KEGG mucin, GO protein secretion, Reactome vesicle budding) despite stable protein levels, suggesting post-translational remodeling of the secretory pathway in IPMNs. Downregulated pathways center on carbohydrate catabolism (GUSB) and nitric oxide regulation (DDAH1), indicating shifts in metabolic and vascular microenvironment processes. Sterol/ cholesterol homeostasis appears subtly suppressed via ERLIN2 and GUSB. Overall, glycosylation rewiring contrasts with broader proteome changes, pinpointing specialized post-translational adaptations in neoplastic ducts.  

Targeted subset  
Keyword-guided filtering underscored:  
- Arginine Catabolic Process (GO:0006527) via DDAH1  
- Cholesterol Homeostasis (MSigDB_Hallmark) via GUSB  
- Sterol Biosynthetic Regulation (GO:0106118) via ERLIN2  

Key Genes/Proteins (leading edge)  

Up:  
| Gene   | Role                    | Pathway(s)                                   |  
|--------|-------------------------|----------------------------------------------|  
| CPD    | Carboxypeptidase D      | Protein Maturation; RHO GTPase Cycle         |  
| TSPAN13| Tetraspanin/adherence   | Vesicle-mediated Transport; Protein Secretion|  

Down:  
| Gene   | Role                      | Pathway(s)                                    |  
|--------|---------------------------|-----------------------------------------------|  
| GUSB   | Lysosomal glycosidase     | Glycosaminoglycan Degradation; Cholesterol Homeostasis |  
| DDAH1  | Methylarginine metabolism | Arginine Catabolism; eNOS Activation          |  
| ERLIN2 | ER-raft lipid sensor      | Sterol Biosynthetic Process; SREBP Signaling  |  
| CPD    | Protease maturation       | Protein Maturation; RHO GTPase Cycle         |  

Comparisons  
- Proteome reveals 3 949 differential proteins (immunoglobulin chains prominent), whereas glycoproteome focuses on secretory machinery and metabolism with only partial overlap.  
- Single-modality glyco signals (e.g., TLR8) absent in proteome denote lower confidence.  

Implications  
- Post-translational glycosylation reprogramming may drive mucin properties and immune interactions in IPMNs.  
- Altered arginine/NO pathways (DDAH1) suggest vascular remodeling.  
- Sterol homeostasis shifts (ERLIN2) implicate membrane microdomain modulation, offering potential statin‐based interventions.  

Next Steps & Clarification  
- Validate CPD, DDAH1, ERLIN2 glyco-changes via targeted MS in independent IPMN samples.  
- Functionally assess O-glycan alterations on mucin viscosity and cyst growth in organoids.  
- Examine NO signaling impact on IPMN stroma by immunohistochemistry for DDAH1 and eNOS.  
- Perform lipidomic profiling to confirm sterol biosynthesis perturbations and SREBP activity.
